answer.evidence: The main body is the stone pedestal, rows 36-45, 12 px wide. Its top face is the light band at rows 36-40 (L about 218-221), 5 rows tall. It ends in a slightly darker edge at row 40-41, and the front face with the blue plaque sits below at rows 41-45 (about 5 rows). The lantern has a sloped blue and gold roof (rows 2-7, widening from 1 to 11 px) above its glass body, so it also reads as a top surface. The thin post needs no top. No isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall lamp about one tile wide, so I judged it mainly by eye and by its measured facts. It has 17 visible tones per full tile, level with prop-stall-cheese (17) and close to prop-well-roofed (20). It has 0% near-flat coverage and 23 distinct colours, more than the thin prop-lamp-crook reference (14). The lantern shows a lit-glass ramp, the gold bands and crown cap carry highlight and shadow, and the pedestal has a lit top face and a shaded front with a plaque, so there are no large flat fills. About 51% of the dark edge pixels are neutral. That is between the near-black lamp-crook (100%) and the tinted hedge and cheese stall (0-1%), so I rate the outline mixed. The post and pedestal show roughly 3-4 steps per material against the references' 5-6, a little shallower but acceptable at this size. Next to the crook lamp it looks richer, not thinner or more sticker-like.
